statement: The two one-dimensional marginal distributions of a random pair (X,Y) determine the joint distribution of (X,Y) uniquely.
ground_truth_witness: On {0,1}^2 compare J1, which puts mass 1/4 on each of the four points (two independent fair bits), with J2, which puts mass 1/2 on (0,0) and 1/2 on (1,1) (one fair bit duplicated). Both joints have identical marginals - X uniform on {0,1} and Y uniform on {0,1} - yet J1 gives the point (0,1) mass 1/4 while J2 gives it mass 0, so distinct joints share the same marginals.
reference_authority: published counterexample (book-cited), verified per partB_feasibility records
book_citation: J. M. Stoyanov, Counterexamples in Probability, Wiley, 1987 (3rd ed., Dover, 2013); sections on distribution functions and independence of random variables (different joint laws with the same marginals); example number not pinned from freely available sources.
